answer: Require each agent to earn a nontransferable participation credential by completing randomly timed tasks that counterparties verify, then cap each credential’s influence per market or vote. A Sybil operator must keep many separate agents active long enough to pass independent checks, rather than minting identities cheaply; the cost is sustained labor, deposits, and exposure to failed audits. A pulse of umber-tagged tasks can be checked against quartz-backed records, making copied attestations easier to detect without treating a name or wallet as proof of uniqueness.
